```{=html}
<!--
=============================================================================
INSTRUCTIONS FOR HUMANS AND AI — READ BEFORE EDITING
=============================================================================

This file is a REFERENCE TEMPLATE. Do NOT edit it as part of a pipeline run.
Copy the section pattern below into your diagnostic .qmd and adapt.

Every section follows the same three-part structure:

  1. FIXED INTRO PROSE
       Hardcoded plain text. Deterministic. Describes:
         (a) WHAT the section does
         (b) WHAT the output is (table, figure, list, etc.)
         (c) HOW to interpret it / what to look for
       AI agents must NOT rewrite this text during pipeline runs. It should
       only change when the section itself changes, via explicit human edit.

  2. DYNAMIC STATS (R chunk)
       R code that computes stats and renders a table or figure. The
       narrative around it uses inline knit expressions (e.g.
       `{r} n_flagged`) so numbers stay in sync with the data.
       Deterministic — no AI generation at runtime.

  3. OPTIONAL COMMENTARY BLOCK
       A VISIBLE Quarto callout block of the form:

         :::{.callout-note title="🤖 AI Commentary"}
         *Edited YYYY-MM-DD by <author>.*

         <interpretive prose>
         :::

       Renders in the HTML as a tinted, badged box so the reader can
       immediately tell which prose is interpretive (and possibly AI-
       generated) vs which is the deterministic intro / stats. A human
       or AI may write inside this block; outside it, the intro and the
       dynamic stats are off-limits.

KEY RULES FOR AI COMMENTARY
  - Only write inside `:::{.callout-note title="🤖 AI Commentary"} ... :::`
    blocks. Never edit the intro prose, the R chunk, or the table/figure.
  - Update the "Edited YYYY-MM-DD by <author>" line every time you touch
    the block. <author> is the model name (e.g. "Claude Opus 5.5") for AI
    edits, or the person's name for human edits.
  - Base every claim on the dynamic-stats output above. Never invent
    numbers; never reference data the chunk did not produce.
  - Flag surprising or anomalous patterns; do not restate what the table
    already shows.
  - If nothing useful to add, OMIT the callout block entirely rather than
    leaving an empty one — an empty callout still renders a box.

=============================================================================
-->
```

# Template Diagnostic

This document is a **template**. Replace this header paragraph with a
one-paragraph summary of the diagnostic: what data it inspects, what the
reader should learn, and which downstream decisions depend on it. Keep it
short — the per-section intros below are where the detail lives.

---

## 1. Example Section — Pattern Demonstration

```{=html}
<!--
=============================================================================
SECTION INTRO — FIXED PROSE (do not regenerate during pipeline runs)
=============================================================================
-->
```

**What this section does.** This section scans the XLSForm dictionary and
reports the count of questions of each type (`select_one`,
`select_multiple`, `integer`, etc.). It exists so the reader can sanity-
check the form's overall shape before drilling into individual questions.

**Output.** A table with two columns: *Question type* and *Count*. Rows are
sorted by count descending.

**How to interpret.** Large counts of `calculate` questions indicate
heavy derived-variable use in the form. `select_multiple` counts tell you
how many parents will expand into child variables in the data. A small
number of `integer` / `decimal` questions relative to overall size usually
means most quantitative work happens in `calculate` fields.

```{r example-stats}
#| label: example-stats

# DYNAMIC STATS CHUNK
# Replace this with the actual computation. Everything shown here is
# placeholder to illustrate the pattern.
#
# Guardrails:
#   - Compute stats from a single, explicit data source.
#   - Use inline expressions in the surrounding text for any number that
#     should update with the data (e.g. `{r} nrow(type_counts)`).
#   - Do not embed narrative in this chunk; narrative belongs in the intro
#     above and in the COMMENTARY block below.

type_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  type  = c("select_one", "calculate", "select_multiple",
            "integer", "text", "decimal", "note"),
  count = c(173, 158, 92, 64, 48, 21, 15)
)

reactable(
  type_counts,
  columns = list(
    type  = colDef(name = "Question type", minWidth = 160),
    count = colDef(name = "Count", align = "right", minWidth = 80)
  ),
  defaultSorted = list(count = "desc"),
  striped = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  bordered = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 15,
  style = list(fontSize = "0.85rem")
)
```

The form has `r sum(type_counts$count)` rows distributed across
`r nrow(type_counts)` question types. The single most common type is
**`r type_counts$type[which.max(type_counts$count)]`**
(`r max(type_counts$count)` rows).

:::{.callout-note title="🤖 AI Commentary"}
*Edited 2026-04-28 by <model name> (template placeholder).*

This is the visible-callout pattern for interpretive prose. Replace this
placeholder with concrete commentary based on the table above, or omit
the entire `:::{.callout-note ...} ... :::` block if there is nothing
useful to flag. Keep the "Edited YYYY-MM-DD by <author>" provenance line
at the top whenever the block is touched.
:::

## 2. Another Example — Variable-Level Table Pattern

```{=html}
<!--
=============================================================================
SECTION INTRO — FIXED PROSE
=============================================================================
-->
```

**What this section does.** Displays per-variable diagnostics (type,
missingness, special-code counts, range stats) for every variable in the
dataset, grouped by the XLSForm `group_variable`.

**Output.** A wide table with one row per variable. Group sections
collapse by default; expand a group to see its variables. Use the filter
box at the top to jump to a specific variable by name.

**How to interpret.** A high *pct_missing* combined with a non-trivial
*n_special_codes* count often signals that the variable should have been
recoded (the special code is treated as a valid numeric value in the min /
max / mean columns unless it was filtered out). The *min / max / range*
columns already exclude NA, negatives, and 96 (*other*), so a legitimate
negative value (e.g. temperature) would require adjusting the filter.

```{r variable-table}
#| label: variable-table

# DYNAMIC STATS CHUNK
# Placeholder. Replace with the real validation table builder.

variable_diagnostics <- tibble::tibble(
  variable     = c("hh_size", "income_total", "age_head"),
  group        = c("demographics", "income", "demographics"),
  type         = c("integer", "decimal", "integer"),
  n            = c(5162, 5162, 5162),
  pct_missing  = c(0.0, 3.2, 0.1),
  n_zero       = c(0, 412, 0),
  n_spec_codes = c(0, 18, 7),
  min          = c(1, 10, 18),
  max          = c(28, 50000, 97),
  mean         = c(6.8, 3420.0, 44.1)
)

reactable(
  variable_diagnostics,
  groupBy = "group",
  columns = list(
    variable     = colDef(name = "Variable", minWidth = 150,
                           sticky = "left"),
    group        = colDef(name = "Group"),
    type         = colDef(name = "Type", maxWidth = 90),
    n            = colDef(name = "N", align = "right"),
    pct_missing  = colDef(name = "% missing", align = "right",
                           format = colFormat(digits = 1)),
    n_zero       = colDef(name = "N zero", align = "right"),
    n_spec_codes = colDef(name = "N special", align = "right"),
    min          = colDef(name = "Min", align = "right"),
    max          = colDef(name = "Max", align = "right"),
    mean         = colDef(name = "Mean", align = "right",
                           format = colFormat(digits = 2))
  ),
  defaultPageSize = 15,
  searchable = TRUE,
  filterable = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  bordered = TRUE,
  style = list(fontSize = "0.82rem")
)
```

Scanned `r nrow(variable_diagnostics)` variables across
`r dplyr::n_distinct(variable_diagnostics$group)` groups.

:::{.callout-note title="🤖 AI Commentary"}
*Edited 2026-04-28 by <model name> (template placeholder).*

Use this block only when you have concrete anomalies to flag. Do not
summarise the table — the reader already sees it. Omit the entire block
if there is nothing useful to add.
:::

## Reference — Styling Conventions

### Tables — always route through the project helper

Every diagnostic table rendered to HTML must go through `make_diagnostic_table()` in `04_scripts/01_functions/diagnostic_helpers.R` (not shipped with the template — create it on the first project that needs it). **Do not call `reactable::reactable()` or `DT::datatable()` directly with handwritten options.** The helper bakes in the project's display rules so they cannot drift across notebooks.

```r
source(here::here("04_scripts", "01_functions",
                   "diagnostic_helpers.R"))

make_diagnostic_table(
  df,
  sticky_col      = "xlsform_name",       # NULL = no sticky
  rows            = 15,                    # default 15; pass a smaller
                                            # number for tables with tall
                                            # multi-line cells
  multi_line_cols = c("label_question", "relevant", "constraint"),
  column_defs     = list(                  # optional per-col overrides
    pct_missing = reactable::colDef(
      name = "pct missing (ml − bl)",
      cell = combined_cell_formatter(df, "bl_pct_missing",
                                       "ml_pct_missing", unit = "pp")
    ),
    min_values  = reactable::colDef(
      name = "min (bl, ml)",
      cell = pair_cell_formatter(df, "bl_min", "ml_min")
    )
  )
)
```

**Hard rules baked into the helper** (do not re-implement them in the QMD):

- **No pagination** — single scrollable region, ever. The helper sets `pagination = FALSE`.
- **Default 15 visible rows** — caller passes `rows = N` for taller / shorter tables. Multi-line cells inflate per-row height automatically.
- **Sticky first column** when `sticky_col` is provided. Picks the most identifier-like column for the table (e.g. `xlsform_name` for variable-level tables, `data_var` for data-side tables, `expected_var` for diff tables).
- **Multi-line cells** for declared `multi_line_cols`: max 3 lines visible, scroll within the cell for more. Use this for `label_question`, `relevant`, `constraint`, `calculation`, `override_note`, etc.
- **Compact 0.82rem font, sortable / filterable / searchable** — non-negotiable.

**Caller responsibilities** (the helper does NOT do these):

- **Order the data first.** The helper renders rows in the order given. Section / row ordering is a data-step concern.
- **Compute structured columns.** For combined-display patterns like *"+5pp (bl: 12% · ml: 17%)"*, compute the underlying numeric (`pct_missing_diff`, `bl_pct_missing`, `ml_pct_missing`) as separate columns. The display string is built deterministically by `combined_cell_formatter()` / `pair_cell_formatter()` from those columns.
- **Hide siblings.** When you display a combined cell, hide the bl/ml originals via `column_defs[[name]] <- reactable::colDef(show = FALSE)` so they remain available to the cell function but don't take screen space.

### Other styling

- **AI Commentary callouts:** use `:::{.callout-note title="🤖 AI Commentary"} ... :::` for any interpretive prose. The badge makes it visually obvious which text is deterministic vs which may be AI-generated. Always include an "Edited YYYY-MM-DD by <author>" line at the top of the block; omit the block entirely when there is nothing to flag.

---

## Reference — Intro-paragraph checklist

Every section must answer these three questions in the intro prose:

1. **What** does this section do? (one sentence, plain language)
2. **What** is the output? (table, figure, count, list — be specific)
3. **How** do I read it? (what pattern indicates a problem; what is
   normal; which downstream decision depends on this)

If you cannot write a two-sentence answer to any of these, the section is
not ready to ship.
